scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Western swing arose in the late 1920s and early 1930s out of house parties, ranch dances, and small-town dance halls across Texas and Oklahoma.
Pioneers like Bob Wills, Milton Brown, and the Light Crust Doughboys blended traditional fiddle tunes with jazz and blues.
By the late 1930s and 1940s, the style achieved massive popularity, broadcasting via powerful radio stations like KVOO and packing ballrooms across the Southwest and California.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Saturday night dances served as the core of social life for working-class communities throughout Texas, Oklahoma, and California, providing a vital recreational outlet amid the hardships of the Great Depression and World War II.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers engaged in simple couples dances, including two-steps and the Lindy Hop, enhanced with Western twirls.
By 1937, the jitterbug gained immense popularity in the West, characterized by a style that was smoother and more subdued than the all-out boogie woogie.
Watch for Western twirl, Western jitterbug.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is performed by a hot string band featuring fiddles, mandolin, upright bass, electric and acoustic guitars, and banjos, frequently augmented by drums, saxophones, trumpets, trombones, pianos, accordion, and the distinctive electrically amplified steel guitar.
Listen for the fiddles, mandolin, upright bass, electric guitars.
The pulse is 2/4 or 4/4.

An amalgamation of rural, cowboy, polka, early honky-tonk, Dixieland jazz, and blues blended with swing, played by a hot string band featuring electrically amplified stringed instruments, especially the steel guitar.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Key figures include Bob Wills, co-founder of the Light Crust Doughboys and leader of the Texas Playboys; Milton Brown, pioneer of Western swing vocal styling; Spade Cooley, bandleader dubbed the 'King of Western Swing'; and Johnnie Lee Wills and Hank Thompson, who carried the tradition forward.

The genre developed distinct regional hubs, originating in the Texas-Oklahoma borderlands and expanding dramatically during World War II into a thriving California scene centered around Los Angeles area ballrooms.
Western swing developed as an outgrowth of country music and jazz.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken
Variant names as a small list

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Western swing is influence of Honky-tonk: Western swing directly influenced the development of honky-tonk music.
Western swing is influence of Rockabilly: Shared rhythm and electrified instrumentation inspired early rockabilly.
Western swing is parent of Jazz: Dixieland and big band swing heavily influenced the genre's harmonic structure and improvisation.
